source.note: Every colour is an RGB triplet custom property (--c-*) consumed as rgb(var(--c-x) / alpha). The hex values in DESIGN.md frontmatter are exact conversions of the dark board (default); light-* keys are the light opt-out.

signal-green.displayName: Signal green (active / in the gym now)

display.purpose: Desktop page title (30px, 36px at >=640px). Hidden on the phone home screen.

headline.purpose: Card and dialog titles; the Due next heading.

title.purpose: Member names in rows, settings section titles, first-run step titles.

body.purpose: Default text, buttons (600), inputs, nav items (500).

label.purpose: Field labels, tabs, strip labels (muted), table cells.

small.purpose: Badges (500), hints, table headers (500 muted), timestamps.

caption.purpose: The one uppercase element: PENDING / ENDING / LAPSED under a board numeral (tracking 0.08em). Also 12px for tab-bar labels and avatar initials without caps or tracking.

led.purpose: Doto 900 'ROND' 20, tabular, line-height 1. Amounts due, days left, counts on the board and stat figures only. Sizes: 24px board rows, 26px strip, 28px strip at >=640px, 22px member list, 18-30px stat figures stepping down with length.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Content cards, secondary buttons, header search. Flat on the dark board.

shadows.name: shadow-pop
shadows.purpose: Every floating layer: dialogs, drawer, toasts, palette, fixed phone actions.

shadows.name: shadow-sheet
shadows.purpose: Layers rising from the bottom edge.

shadows.name: button-primary
shadows.purpose: Key-cap highlight and short drop on the crimson button.

shadows.name: inset-ring-active
shadows.purpose: Active nav item and active tab-bar slot.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: :focus-visible on every control (Tailwind ring-2 ring-accent/70 ring-offset-2 ring-offset-canvas).

shadows.name: input-focus
shadows.purpose: Input focus ring with border at ink/60.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Scrim behind dialogs and the drawer.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: .pressable on every button, row, nav item. Reduced motion: scale 1, 0ms.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: background, border, color, box-shadow, opacity on .pressable; input border and ring.

motion.name: springSheet
motion.purpose: Bottom sheets and the drawer sliding in; drag snap-back.

motion.name: fadeReduced
motion.purpose: Overlay fades, and the replacement for every transition under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global collapse; motion/react paths also switch to fadeReduced and disable drag.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Display 30 -> 36px, strip LED 26 -> 28px, page padding 16 -> 24px, tables replace row cards, toasts move bottom-right, dialogs centre.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar + page header appear; bottom tab bar, drawer and fixed phone actions disappear; home grid becomes 2/3 + 1/3.

breakpoints.name: contrast-more
breakpoints.purpose: Muted, faint and hairlines step up in contrast.

narrative.overview:
GymBook is the departures board the gym owner reads every morning at the desk, usually on a phone, one-handed. The ground is near-black; panels are a step lighter charcoal separated by hairlines rather than shadows; the ink is off-white. Nothing on the board is decorative: a row is a name, a reason, and a number that counts down, and the number is set in a dot-matrix face so it reads like a lit display. Colour is reserved for signal. Each signal colour has exactly one meaning (red is money pending, amber is a plan ending inside seven days, green is active or in the gym right now, blue is a plan that starts later), and brand crimson appears only on the primary action and the logo.

Density is a desk register, not a marketing page: 52 px rows, 20 px card padding, a single 8 px grid, right-aligned numerals in one column. Hierarchy comes from size and ink level (ink, muted, faint), never from colour or weight alone; headings sit at 600, labels at 500, body at 400. Controls are the standard web controls, 36 px on a pointer device and 44 px on a touch screen.

The board is the default and the only theme the system follows on its own. The light theme is the same roles translated to a cool light board (white panels, cool grey canvas, darker signal colours) and is reached only by the owner's stored opt-out; the app does not follow the operating system's colour scheme. Rejected: four equal stat cards above a chart, uppercase kickers and eyebrow labels, and decorative gradients or glows.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black board with charcoal panels and 1 px hairlines; tonal steps carry depth, floating layers get one soft shadow.
One interface face (Barlow Semi Condensed) and one signature numeral face (Doto dot-matrix, weight 900) used only where the board counts down.
Signal colours are jobs, not moods: red, amber, green, blue each mean one thing everywhere.
Crimson is brand and primary action only; it never carries status.
Sentence case throughout; the only uppercase in the system is the 12 px caption under a board numeral.
8 px spacing grid, 52 px board rows, 36/44 px controls, 10 px control radius, 14 px card radius.
Motion is a critically damped spring (no overshoot) or a 150 ms ease-out; reduced motion collapses it all to a 150 ms cross-fade.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Red means money pending, amber means ending within 7 days, green means active or present now, blue means starts later. A signal colour never appears for any other reason, and no second colour is ever added to say the same thing.

rules.name: The Crimson Is Not a Signal Rule
rules.body: Brand crimson belongs to the primary action, the logo and the focus ring. Status, errors and overdue amounts use signal red, which is a different hue.

rules.name: The Soft Tint Rule
rules.body: A -soft colour only ever sits directly behind its own signal colour (badge, banner, error box). It is not a card, section or hover background.

rules.name: The Lit Numeral Rule
rules.body: The dot-matrix face is for what the board counts: amounts due, days left, counts on the board and stat figures. Money in prose, invoice totals, deltas and table cells stay in Barlow with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every heading, button, label, badge and nav item is sentence case. The only uppercase is the 12 px tracked caption under a board numeral; no kickers, eyebrows or section-label caps anywhere else.

rules.name: The Ink Level Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside a component is ink → muted → faint, with size; weight stays within 400–600 and is never pushed to 700+.

rules.name: The Hairline Depth Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest are flat and bordered; a shadow means the layer floats above the page and can be dismissed.

dos: Do give each signal colour one job only: red for money pending, amber for ending within 7 days, green for active or in the gym now, blue for starts later.
Do keep crimson for the primary action, the logo and the focus ring; use signal red, not crimson, for anything overdue or destructive.
Do set amounts due, days left, board counts and stat figures in the .led numeral face (Doto 900, 'ROND' 20), right-aligned in one column, and keep every other number in Barlow with tabular figures.
Do build depth from the tonal steps (deep → canvas → surface → raised) and 1 px hairlines; reserve the pop shadow for layers that float and dismiss.
Do keep controls at 36 px on a fine pointer and 44 px on a coarse pointer, with 16 px input text on touch; use .h-control* rather than hard-coded heights.
Do write everything in sentence case, 400–600 weight, with hierarchy from size and ink level.
Do ship the dark board as the default and keep light as a stored opt-out via data-theme='light'; translate roles, never invent light-only colours.
Do use the motion tokens (0.3 s / 0.4 s springs with zero bounce, 150 ms ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)) and let prefers-reduced-motion collapse them to a cross-fade.
donts: Don't add uppercase kickers, eyebrows or tracked section labels; the only uppercase is the caption under a board numeral.
Don't use a -soft tint as a card, section or hover background, or colour a whole row or card by status; status lives in the numeral, the badge or the summary text.
Don't arrange the home screen as four equal stat cards above a chart; the board leads and today's figures sit in one hairline-divided strip.
Don't put shadows on content cards on the dark board, and never use hard offset or coloured shadows anywhere.
Don't use the dot-matrix face for prose amounts, invoice totals, deltas, table cells or decorative numbers.
